subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: Should OpenClaw add a core/plugin-API provenance chain for durable state writes and reads, and if so what metadata may be persisted and exposed to plugins?
rationale: This cannot be safely resolved by automation because it defines security boundaries, public plugin hook contracts, durable state schema, and read-time trust policy.

options.title: Design minimal provenance API first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies durable metadata, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and read-time policy before any code PR.

options.title: Scope to narrower hooks
options.body: Split implementation across the existing before_tool_call and before_persistence_write issues, leaving this issue as the umbrella until both land.

options.title: Defer beyond core
options.body: Decide that current plugin/memory surfaces are enough for now and leave advanced taint tracking to external plugins until a concrete missing API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design minimal provenance API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies durable metadata, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and read-time policy before any code PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent transcript and memory-corpus ownership is closest to the durable state boundary this decision would change.
